text:
DONE for the ceiling, which is the part that made large batches hostile to a shared login node. True batching is scoped to G3 for the reason below.

RemoteExchangeBudget is a shared semaphore that handles queue behind before every remote exchange. RemoteBatchOptions and RemoteScriptBatchOptions gained maximumConcurrentExchanges (default 8), one budget is created per batch submission, and every element handle shares it — for both registered and script batches, and across both the result read and the accounting probe.

The measured problem was concrete: ADR 0003 deliberately gives each request its own SSH process instead of multiplexing, and RemoteBatch awaits with elements.parTraverse(_.await), so each element ran its own polling loop. A 100-element batch opened 100 simultaneous SSH processes per tick; the 4,096-job figure in docs/acceptance/p5-site-scale.md described the MANAGED coordinator's batched path, not this one. Now the count is bounded by configuration regardless of batch size.

A lone handle passes RemoteExchangeBudget.unbounded, since it can only have one exchange in flight anyway and a ceiling would be pure overhead. Tested in both directions: a budget of 4 never admits more than 4 simultaneous exchanges across 32 concurrent callers, an unbounded budget does NOT serialize, and all 50 of 50 queued exchanges still run — the budget queues, it never drops.

WHAT THIS IS NOT, stated plainly because the bead asked for batching: this is a ceiling, not batching. Genuinely batching result reads means one exchange returning several results, which requires a new protocol method and is therefore a wire change. That belongs with G3's batched-read work, and doing it here would have meant designing the wire twice. The ceiling needed no protocol change and fixes the operational hazard on its own.

Also unchanged, and correctly so: the durable controller keeps its own authority. This bounds convenience handles; ObservationCoordinator's batched observation path is untouched.

Verification: 3 new tests. Full suite 432 green, zero warnings under -Werror, scalafmt clean.
